narrative: Conducted a full-day digital literacy session with 52 smallholder potato farmers in Musanze district. Participants were trained on how to use the AIBID mobile data collection tool to log yield data, input costs, and market prices. Connectivity was intermittent during morning hours but stabilised by afternoon. Notable finding: 78% of farmers already owned smartphones (Tecno or Itel brand) but most had never used data entry apps. Demonstration of voice query feature in Kinyarwanda prompted strong excitement — participants requested a voice-first interface for future versions. Three farmers volunteered as community data champions to assist peers.
key_findings: High smartphone ownership but low app literacy
Kinyarwanda voice interface critical for adoption
Strong interest in market price alerts
Need for offline-first data sync capability
issues_found: Intermittent 4G connectivity (MTN network gaps)
Literacy barriers for 8 participants requiring pictographic support
Power supply unreliable at training venue
recommendations: Prioritise offline sync feature in next AIBID mobile update
Develop pictographic onboarding guide in Kinyarwanda
Partner with local cooperative to appoint 3 community data champions per sector

narrative: Conducted a data quality audit of cattle registration records submitted by 12 cooperatives in Nyagatare district over Q4 2023. Cross-referenced MINAGRI paper records against AIBID platform entries. Found significant data quality issues: 23% of livestock records had missing veterinary certificate dates, 17% had GPS coordinates outside plausible district boundaries (likely coordinate entry errors), and 8 records had duplicate animal IDs. The data cleaning process took 4 hours on-site working with cooperative treasurers to reconcile discrepancies. All 12 cooperatives now have corrected records uploaded. One cooperative (Karama Cattle Coop) had completely reversed latitude/longitude values for all 45 of their entries.
key_findings: 23% missing veterinary data
17% GPS coordinate errors
Duplicate animal IDs in 8 records
Karama Coop had systematically reversed lat/lon values
issues_found: Paper-to-digital transcription errors
Lack of GPS validation at point of entry
Cooperative staff turnover causing data inconsistency
recommendations: Implement GPS boundary validation in AIBID mobile app
Add mandatory veterinary date field
Create cooperative data steward certification program
Quarterly data audits per district

narrative: Visited Rulindo Farmers SACCO to onboard them onto the AIBID financial analytics platform. The SACCO has 847 members and RWF 245 million in total savings. Initial data migration from their Excel-based system was completed remotely the week prior. Today's visit focused on training the 4 SACCO staff members on the dashboard, report generation, and credit risk scoring features. The loan officer, Mr. Habimana Jean, was particularly engaged with the delinquency trend chart which immediately revealed that loans disbursed in October 2023 had a 12% higher 30-day delinquency rate than prior cohorts — this pattern had not been visible in their manual review process. The SACCO manager committed to reviewing all October-cohort loans by end of January.
key_findings: October 2023 loan cohort shows 12% higher delinquency — first time detected
SACCO staff lack basic data interpretation skills despite good interest
Manual Excel tracking masked critical portfolio quality trends
Dashboard adoption was immediate once credit risk charts were shown
issues_found: Internet speed too slow for real-time dashboard refresh (2G connection)
SACCO staff need ongoing coaching, not just one-off training
Outdated laptop hardware making AIBID interface slow
recommendations: Install AIBID Lite offline version for low-bandwidth environments
Schedule monthly 2-hour coaching sessions for SACCO staff
Provide minimum hardware requirements to SACCOs before onboarding

narrative: Conducted training for 78 Community Health Workers (Inararibonye) across 6 health centres in Huye district. Training covered use of the AIBID mobile dashboard for tracking household health visits, reporting malnutrition cases, and logging maternal health check-ins. The Ministry of Health supervisor, Dr. Claudine Mukamurigo, attended the afternoon session and was impressed by the real-time aggregation showing the entire district's health data on a single screen. One CHW, Immaculée from Mbazi sector, raised an important question: she visits households without network and currently cannot submit reports until she returns to the health centre. The offline sync feature needs urgent prioritisation. By end of day, all 78 CHWs had successfully submitted at least one test health report through the system.
key_findings: 78/78 CHWs successfully onboarded in single day
Ministry of Health supervisor expressed strong satisfaction
Offline data collection is the single biggest adoption blocker
District-level aggregation view was particularly impressive to supervisors
issues_found: No offline data collection capability in current version
Some CHW phones (3G only) struggle with dashboard loading time
Kinyarwanda labels needed for all data fields — some CHWs cannot read French/English
recommendations: Offline mode must be shipped in next 60 days — critical for health sector
Full Kinyarwanda localisation of all mobile interface elements
Light-weight mode for 3G devices

narrative: Conducted quarterly site assessment and user review at Bank of Kigali headquarters. Met with the data analytics team (12 people) and the credit risk department (6 people). Platform usage has grown 34% quarter-over-quarter with 210 active users now versus 156 in Q3 2023. The credit scoring model has been live for 9 months and has processed 48,500 loan applications. The model's Gini coefficient is 0.68, significantly above the 0.52 benchmark from their previous manual scoring. Key expansion request: BK wants AIBID to integrate with their core banking system (T24 Temenos) for automated loan decisioning without manual dashboard visits. This is a $120k additional scope opportunity. Also discussed BK's interest in extending the contract by an additional 3 years.
key_findings: 34% QoQ growth in platform usage
Gini coefficient 0.68 vs 0.52 benchmark — strong credit model performance
48,500 loan applications processed by AI model
T24 Temenos integration is a $120k opportunity
3-year renewal interest expressed
issues_found: API integration with T24 Temenos is technically complex
BK IT team concerned about data security of API calls
Report export to PDF has formatting issues in some browsers
recommendations: Engage BK IT and Temenos team for API scoping workshop
Security audit for API integration
Fix PDF export formatting bug — escalate to engineering

narrative: Visited Gorilla's Nest Lodge and Bisate Lodge (Wilderness Safaris) for initial onboarding of AIBID analytics platform for the Rwanda Tourism sector pilot. Both properties expressed strong interest in occupancy prediction and guest sentiment analytics. Initial data collection revealed that neither property had a structured guest data management system — guest information was split across WhatsApp messages, email threads, and a handwritten ledger. This will require a 4-week data preparation phase before platform onboarding can proceed. The Bisate Lodge manager, Ms. Sarah Kamana, specifically requested a feature showing how weather data correlates with tourist booking patterns — she believes this would help them manage staff rostering better.
key_findings: Tourism sector has severe data maturity gaps
No structured guest data management at either property
Guest data fragmented across WhatsApp, email, and paper ledger
Weather-booking correlation analytics is a key use case for hospitality
issues_found: 4-week data preparation phase needed before onboarding
No existing CRM or PMS (Property Management System)
GDPR-equivalent data privacy concerns for international guests
recommendations: Develop lightweight data collection template for hospitality sector
Integrate weather API data feed as standard in AIBID
Consult with Rwanda Development Board on tourism data standards
Consider hospitality-specific AIBID module as product extension

narrative: Conducted a pilot assessment visit to Rwamagana district education office and 5 secondary schools for the potential AIBID education analytics deployment. Met with the District Education Officer and principals of 5 schools. Current state: attendance is tracked on paper registers, exam results are entered into an Excel file once per term, and there is no systematic analysis of learning outcomes. The District Education Officer was shown a demo using anonymised data from a similar district in Kenya — the dropout prediction model generated significant interest, particularly the ability to identify at-risk students 8 weeks before they drop out. Consent and data protection procedures discussed extensively. Three schools agreed to participate in a 90-day data collection pilot starting March 2024.
key_findings: District has no digital data infrastructure — entirely paper-based
DEO highly motivated to adopt analytics but lacks technical staff
Dropout prediction demo was the highest-impact use case demonstrated
Data protection concerns need clear framework before proceeding
issues_found: No existing digital data to onboard — data collection starts from scratch
Insufficient ICT staff in district education office
Data privacy framework for minors not yet defined
recommendations: Develop data collection starter kit for education sector
Clarify REB (Rwanda Education Board) policy on student data use
Start 90-day pilot with volunteer schools
Create simple Excel upload templates as interim solution

narrative: Monthly operational review at Inyange Industries' main production facility in Kicukiro. Reviewed three months of production efficiency data now flowing through AIBID. Key insight surfaced: the 6AM-9AM production window consistently shows 23% lower throughput than the 9AM-3PM window — analysis suggests this correlates with the morning temperature-dependent viscosity of dairy products in the processing line. The quality control module flagged 3 batches in January with abnormal pH readings 4 hours before they would have reached packaging — all 3 were caught and recycled, avoiding an estimated RWF 8 million in losses. The Operations Director has now formally requested that AIBID be integrated into their ERP (SAP Business One). This is a major technical integration opportunity.
key_findings: 6AM-9AM throughput 23% lower — likely temperature-viscosity correlation
AI caught 3 defective batches early — saved RWF 8M in waste
Operations Director requesting SAP Business One integration
Production anomaly detection model achieving 91% precision
issues_found: SAP integration requires 3-month scoping and development
IoT sensor data from production line not yet available — manual entry still required
Staff resist entering data during shift due to time pressure
recommendations: Scope SAP Business One integration — potential $80k project
Install IoT data gateway to automate production readings
Train line supervisors on quick-entry mobile interface
Present ROI case to board: RWF 8M saved in first quarter

narrative: Surveyed 124 soybean farming households across 4 cooperatives in Muhanga district for the GIZ-funded AgriData project. Used the AIBID mobile data collection tool with the new offline mode (beta version 2.3). The offline mode performed well — all 124 surveys were collected without network connection and synced successfully when within 2km of Muhanga town. Survey captured: land size, yield, input costs, selling price, buyer type, and mobile money access. Preliminary analysis on-device showed that households selling through cooperatives received on average 28% higher prices than those selling to individual traders. This data point will be central to the GIZ report. One interesting outlier: a single farmer in Rongi sector reported a yield of 45 tonnes per hectare (the district average is 1.8 tonnes) — likely a data entry error in the measurement unit field.
key_findings: Offline mode (beta v2.3) functioned successfully across 124 surveys
Cooperative sellers receive 28% higher prices than individual traders
Clear data entry error detected: 45T/ha yield is ~25x normal — data cleaning required
Mobile money access is 89% among surveyed households
issues_found: One extreme outlier in yield data (45T/ha) — needs correction
Some questions on input costs were misunderstood — need clearer phrasing
4 phones ran out of battery during long survey day — need power banks
recommendations: Add field-level validation rules to prevent extreme outliers
Simplify input cost question to per-bag rather than per-hectare
Purchase 10 power banks for field officers

narrative: Collected malaria surveillance data from 8 health centres in Gakenke district as part of the Rwanda Biomedical Centre AI project. Monthly malaria case counts, treatment outcomes, and bed net distribution records were manually entered into AIBID from paper registers. The data showed an unusual spike in malaria cases in Ruli sector during December 2023 — 340 cases versus a monthly average of 85. The RBC district health supervisor confirmed this was real and was attributed to a delay in insecticide spraying. The AIBID prediction model, running on the previous 18 months of data, had actually flagged Ruli sector as high-risk in November 2023, but the alert was not acted upon. This is a critical finding about alert follow-through. Recommendation: malaria alerts should automatically notify district health supervisors via SMS, not only appear on the dashboard.
key_findings: Ruli sector had 4x normal malaria cases in December — confirmed real outbreak
AIBID prediction model correctly flagged Ruli as high-risk in November — alert ignored
Alert not actioned because supervisor did not check dashboard proactively
Automatic SMS alerts would have enabled earlier response
issues_found: Dashboard-only alerts are insufficient — supervisors don't log in daily
Paper-to-digital data entry creates 4-6 week lag in surveillance data
Retrospective data entry means model works on outdated information
recommendations: Implement SMS/WhatsApp alert system for high-risk health predictions
Partner with RBC to mandate weekly digital data submission from health centres
Develop mobile-first data entry for health workers to eliminate paper lag
Present this case study to RBC leadership as evidence for system-wide change

narrative: Visited 89 mango farming households across 5 sectors in Kayonza district to map the mango value chain for the AGRA project. This was a mixed-method visit: structured survey data collected via AIBID mobile tool, supplemented by 12 in-depth oral interviews recorded as voice memos and later transcribed. Key findings: 67% of farmers sell at farm gate (lowest price point), 22% sell at Kayonza market, and only 11% access Kigali or export markets. The main barrier to market access is transport (cited by 78% of respondents) followed by lack of buyers' contact information (cited by 54%). An interesting use case emerged: one progressive farmer, Emmanuel Habimana, had been using the AIBID SMS price query system independently for 8 months and now consistently gets 40% higher prices by timing his harvests to market demand. He became a spontaneous case study for the rest of the group.
key_findings: 67% of farmers only access lowest-value market (farm gate)
Transport cost is primary barrier to better market access
AIBID SMS price query user achieves 40% higher prices — compelling case study
Potential for buyer-farmer digital matchmaking platform
issues_found: Voice memo transcription is manual and slow — 3 hours for 12 interviews
AIBID mobile does not have video or audio recording — limits qualitative data
No export market data available in AIBID for this commodity
recommendations: Develop audio/video data collection option in AIBID mobile
Build Rwanda export market price feed into platform
Pilot buyer-farmer matching feature for 3 value chains in Kayonza
Package Emmanuel Habimana story as marketing case study

activity_type: District Performance Review with Local Administration
narrative: Attended the monthly district performance review meeting chaired by the Nyanza District Mayor. For the first time, the district's development performance was presented using AIBID dashboards projected on a screen — previously all presentations used static PowerPoint slides. The Mayor expressed particular interest in the Imihigo (government performance commitments) progress tracker, which shows real-time completion rates against annual targets. The health sector dashboard sparked the most discussion: the Mayor noticed that Busasamana sector consistently underperforms on nutrition indicators and immediately directed the sector executive to provide a written explanation by next month. This is exactly the kind of evidence-based governance use case we want to showcase. The meeting was attended by 28 district officials, sector executives, and government representatives.
key_findings: First AIBID-powered district performance review meeting in Rwanda
Imihigo tracker generated immediate actionable decisions from Mayor
Health nutrition data prompted immediate governance action
28 officials now have direct exposure to AIBID platform
issues_found: Projector was not bright enough for daylight boardroom — display was hard to read
Some charts have too much data density for non-technical audience
Internet disconnected mid-meeting — offline mode would have saved the presentation
recommendations: Add presentation mode to AIBID with simplified high-contrast visualisations
Pre-load dashboard data before critical meetings in case of connectivity issues
Package this as a case study: AIBID enabling evidence-based district governance
Propose AIBID District Executive Package to all 30 Rwanda districts

narrative: Facilitated a half-day analytics workshop for 38 startup founders at kLab (Kigali's premier tech incubator). Workshop focused on how to use the AIBID data platform to understand customer analytics, financial modelling, and investor reporting. Participants included founders from 14 startups across fintech, agritech, healthtech, and e-commerce sectors. The session included a live demo where a healthtech startup CEO uploaded her customer CSV and asked AIBID a voice query: 'What percentage of my customers returned within 30 days?' — the system processed the query and returned an accurate 67% retention rate with a bar chart in under 8 seconds. The room erupted in applause. Seven startups signed up for the AIBID Startup Tier (free for 6 months, subsidised by Mastercard Foundation partnership).
key_findings: Live voice query demo was the single most impactful moment of entire workshop
7 out of 38 startups signed up on the spot
Startups are underserved by analytics tools — major untapped market
kLab partnership opens access to 200+ early-stage companies
issues_found: Startup Tier product packaging is not fully defined yet
Pricing model for post-subsidy period unclear to new signups
Workshop room capacity limited to 40 — could easily have filled 100 seats
recommendations: Define and publish AIBID Startup Tier pricing and feature set
Plan monthly kLab workshops — high conversion potential
Explore similar partnerships with Growth Africa, Norrsken Kigali, and BPN Rwanda
Use the 'voice query in 8 seconds' demo as hero moment in all sales presentations

narrative: Visited the Kirehe Umwagiliwa irrigation scheme, one of Rwanda's largest, to assess feasibility of deploying AIBID for water usage monitoring and crop yield prediction. The scheme covers 1,200 hectares and serves 215 farming households. Currently, water allocation and irrigation scheduling are managed manually by scheme operators using a paper logbook. No electronic records of water flow, crop growth stages, or soil moisture exist. A drone survey was conducted (photos shared separately) showing crop health across the scheme using NDVI imagery. This visual data, combined with weather station readings, could form the basis of an AI-powered irrigation advisory model. The scheme manager, Mr. Gakuru, was enthusiastic but concerned about the maintenance cost of any IoT sensors. We proposed a low-cost approach using satellite data + mobile phone reports from scheme operators.
key_findings: 1200 ha irrigation scheme with zero digital data systems
NDVI drone imagery shows significant crop health variation across scheme
Satellite data can substitute for expensive IoT sensors — low-cost path to digital monitoring
Scheme manager supportive but needs budget justification for investment
issues_found: Zero baseline digital data — implementation would take 6 months minimum
Satellite data access is expensive at commercial rates
Mobile network coverage in parts of scheme is poor (2G only)
recommendations: Apply for MINAGRI data digitisation grant to cover implementation cost
Partner with Rwanda Space Agency for subsidised satellite data access
Develop a 6-month implementation roadmap with phased milestones
Submit case study proposal to GIZ for agricultural IoT pilot funding

narrative: Attended the quarterly business review meeting with MTN Rwanda's data analytics team and senior leadership. AIBID platform usage has reached 145 active users across the analytics, network operations, and MoMo business units. The churn prediction model is now fully integrated into MTN's CRM workflow — when a customer reaches a churn risk score above 0.75, a retention offer is automatically triggered via the MTN customer service team. This integration has reduced voluntary churn by 14.3% compared to the control group in a randomised A/B test run over 3 months. The VP of Data confirmed that MTN Group in Johannesburg has been informed of the Rwanda implementation and is evaluating a group-wide rollout to 19 countries. This is a $4M+ potential group contract. MTN Rwanda renewal is confirmed for 3 years at a 20% price increase.

MTN Group Johannesburg evaluating pan-African AIBID rollout (19 countries)
$4M+ group contract potential
3-year renewal confirmed at 20% price increase

MoMo transaction data volume is 10x larger than current AIBID data processing capacity
Need to upgrade data pipeline infrastructure for group-scale workloads
recommendations: Initiate engagement with MTN Group CDO in Johannesburg — priority account
Begin infrastructure scoping for 10x data volume capacity upgrade
Prepare MTN Group pitch deck and ROI calculator based on Rwanda results

narrative: Conducted a pilot water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) data collection exercise across 6 water schemes in Burera district, partnering with the Rwanda Water and Forestry Authority (RWFA). This pilot tests whether AIBID's mobile data collection tool can replace the existing WASH monitoring paper forms. Data collected: water source type, daily flow rate (litres), chlorine residual level, number of household connections, and reported breakdowns. The AIBID data collection form worked well for structured fields, but the breakdown narrative field requires long-form text that is difficult to type on a smartphone — voice input would dramatically improve data quality here. GPS tagging of each water point was the most highly valued feature by RWFA staff, who previously had to manually record coordinates in a separate notebook.
key_findings: GPS tagging of water points was the most appreciated new feature
Narrative fields are difficult to complete on smartphone — voice input essential
Daily flow rate data reveals 3 schemes operating below 50% capacity
RWFA staff took to mobile tool quickly — trained in under 30 minutes
issues_found: Narrative/comment fields are difficult to type on touchscreen keyboards
AIBID does not support photo attachment for breakdown documentation
3 water schemes below 50% capacity but cause not captured in structured fields
recommendations: Add voice-to-text for all narrative fields in AIBID mobile
Enable photo attachment with geo-tagged timestamps
Develop WASH-specific data collection template as sector module
Propose RWFA national deployment — estimated 450 water schemes nationwide

narrative: Assessed AIBID data collection feasibility with 167 coffee farmers across 5 cooperatives in Gisagara, which produces some of Rwanda's highest-quality specialty coffee (Bourbon cultivar). Current data challenge: each cooperative tracks cherry collection volumes in a handwritten register, and the central washing station has no digital record of processing parameters (fermentation time, washing duration, drying days). These parameters have direct impact on cup quality scores, which determine export price. We demonstrated how AIBID could create a digital processing log that links field data (farmer, plot, cherry weight) to washing station parameters and eventual export price. If implemented, this would create end-to-end traceability data that specialty coffee buyers (e.g., Blue Bottle Coffee, Intelligentsia) pay a significant premium for. Estimated premium: 15-25% per kg if traceability can be certified.
key_findings: No digital data exists linking farmer to processing to export — massive traceability gap
Blockchain-ready traceability data could earn 15-25% premium on specialty coffee exports
167 farmers are potential beneficiaries of price premium
Cooperatives are willing to adopt digital systems if they see direct income benefit
issues_found: Washing station has no power supply for laptop or tablet
Cooperative data management currently handled by volunteers with no compensation
Coffee harvest is seasonal — 4-month window to collect annual data
recommendations: Develop AIBID Coffee Traceability Module with solar-powered tablet
Explore partnership with CQI (Coffee Quality Institute) for certification
Apply for Rwanda Coffee Board grant for cooperative digitisation
Fast-track implementation to capture the upcoming May harvest season

narrative: Conducted a feasibility assessment for using AIBID's data platform to monitor Lake Kivu's environmental indicators in partnership with the Lake Kivu Monitoring Programme (LKMP). Lake Kivu contains an unusual quantity of dissolved methane and carbon dioxide, making it both a renewable energy resource (Rwanda extracts methane for electricity through KivuWatt) and a potential environmental risk. Current monitoring involves 4 research buoys transmitting sensor data via satellite. The AIBID platform could serve as the central data aggregation and visualisation layer for this data. We reviewed the existing API documentation from the buoy manufacturer — the data format is compatible with AIBID's data ingestion framework. A visualisation demo built live during the meeting showed dissolved methane concentration over time, which the LKMP director immediately wanted printed for a presentation to the Minister of Environment.
key_findings: Lake Kivu buoy API is compatible with AIBID data ingestion framework
Real-time methane monitoring visualisation generated immediate demand
Environmental monitoring is a new, high-value vertical for AIBID
KivuWatt energy company is a potential client for operational data analytics
issues_found: Satellite data transmission has 2-4 hour latency — not truly real-time
API rate limits on buoy data feed need negotiation with manufacturer
Regulatory approval needed to publish environmental data publicly
recommendations: Build Lake Kivu monitoring pilot as a flagship environmental showcase
Engage KivuWatt for commercial energy analytics contract
Apply for UNDP Climate Action grant for environmental monitoring expansion
Package this as AIBID Environmental Analytics vertical

narrative: Visited Irembo (Rwanda's e-government platform) and three e-commerce startups (Afrimart, Konvey, and Covas) in Kigali's Remera tech hub. Afrimart, an online marketplace for Rwandan artisans, expressed interest in using AIBID to understand buyer behaviour, seasonal demand patterns, and price elasticity across product categories. Their current data situation: they have transaction logs in MongoDB but no analytics capability. AIBID's MongoDB connector (planned for Q3 2024) would be the primary integration path. Konvey, a same-day delivery startup, wants route optimisation and delivery performance analytics. Their challenge is real-time data — they need analytics updated every 15 minutes, not daily. This is technically feasible but would require a dedicated streaming data pipeline. Covas, a digital payments startup, declined to share data citing regulatory concerns — potential future opportunity.
key_findings: E-commerce sector has rich transactional data but zero analytics capability
MongoDB connector (Q3 2024) is critical enabler for this sector
Real-time analytics (15-min updates) required for delivery operations — streaming pipeline needed
Regulatory concerns are primary blocker for fintech data sharing
issues_found: AIBID currently supports daily data updates only — insufficient for real-time use cases
MongoDB is not yet a supported data source — limits e-commerce market penetration
Data privacy and regulatory framework unclear for private sector data sharing
recommendations: Accelerate MongoDB connector development — Q3 target must hold
Develop streaming analytics capability roadmap — Q1 2025 target
Work with RURA on a data sharing regulatory sandbox for startups
Propose Afrimart as design partner for e-commerce analytics module

narrative: Compiled the annual field operations review for January–April 2024 based on 19 field visit reports and follow-up data from all active field officers. Key aggregate findings: Total beneficiaries reached through field activities: 763 individuals. Field reports submitted: 19. Districts visited: 14 out of 30. Data quality issues flagged: 3 out of 19 reports (16% data quality flag rate). Sentiment distribution: Very Positive (5), Positive (9), Cautiously Positive (2), Neutral (1), Mixed (1), Excellent (1). The offline sync feature was the most frequently cited missing capability (appeared in 7 of 19 reports). The Kinyarwanda language interface was the second most cited gap (5 reports). Overall field activity in 2024 has shown a 34% increase in beneficiary reach compared to the same period in 2023, driven by the GIZ AgriData project and the Rwanda Biomedical Centre CHW training. The most impactful single intervention was the CHW training in Huye: all 78 CHWs successfully onboarded in a single day. The most strategically significant finding was the MTN churn reduction proof, which has opened a $4M+ group contract opportunity.

16% data quality flag rate (below 20% target — good)
Offline sync mentioned as missing in 7 out of 19 reports — top engineering priority
Kinyarwanda interface missing — cited 5 times — critical for rural adoption
34% increase in beneficiary reach vs Jan-Apr 2023
MTN churn proof is the most commercially significant finding of the period
issues_found: 14 districts visited out of 30 — 16 districts have no field presence
Tourism, manufacturing, and environmental sectors are underdeveloped verticals
No systematic mechanism to translate field insights into product roadmap updates

Launch Kinyarwanda localisation project — engage Perpétue Umubyeyi (R&D NLP) immediately
